statement: The assertion that every planar iid nonnegative nearest-neighbor FPP law has no bigeodesic is false: for the iid point mass at 1, the path gamma(k)=(k,0), k in Z, is a bigeodesic.
assumptions: every edge weight is identically 1; this is an iid law
bigeodesic means every finite segment minimizes total passage time

source.ranking_quote: 5,P0117,Absence of bi-infinite geodesics in planar iid FPP,attempted_un,no bigeodesics in planar iid FPP

proof: Between (m,0) and (n,0), every nearest-neighbor path has at least |n-m| edges and hence passage time at least |n-m|. The horizontal segment attains this value for every pair m<n.
remaining_gap: No gap in the elementary argument identified; independent audit pending. This example has atoms and is not a counterexample to an atomless FPP conjecture.

statement: For a stationary measurable field of finite nonnegative weights on nearest-neighbor Z^2, let A be vertices on self-avoiding bigeodesics; B_n=[-n,n]^2 intersect Z^2; and D_n the vertices in B_n on ANY self-avoiding globally minimizing finite path with both endpoints in partial B_2n. Then E|D_n|/|B_n| tends to P(0 in A). In particular all bigeodesics are absent almost surely exactly when E|D_n|=o(n^2).
assumptions: self-avoiding geodesics minimize over the full lattice, not a confined box
D_n uses all geodesics in case of ties
proof: Centered length-2m geodesic events H_m(v) decrease; a finitely branching prefix tree proves their intersection equals {v in A}. Deterministically A intersect B_n is contained in D_n, which is contained in {v in B_n: H_n(v)}. Stationarity and continuity from above yield p <= E|D_n|/|B_n| <= P(H_n(0)) decreasing to p. Countability of Z^2 gives global absence iff p=0.
remaining_gap: The iid estimate E|D_n|=o(n^2) remains unproved; the independently checked reduction does not solve P0117.

statement: Let T_0 be the union of all infinite simple geodesic rays from 0 in nearest-neighbor Z^2 and q(x)=P(x in T_0). For S_n={x:||x||_infinity=n}, sum_{x in S_n}q(x)>=P(T_0 nonempty). If a ray exists almost surely, the shell sum is at least 1 for every n and sup_{x in S_n}q(x)>=1/(8n). Consequently neither vanishing shell incidence nor uniform q=o(1/n) is available in that setting.
assumptions: rays are simple nearest-neighbor infinite paths from 0

proof: Every infinite simple ray leaves the finite box B_(n-1) and first exits at a vertex in S_n. Thus |T_0 intersect S_n|>=1_{T_0 nonempty}; take expectations and use |S_n|=8n. Standard positive iid finite-weight FPP supplies rays via finite-minimizer compactness; that auxiliary derivation is in ATTEMPT.md.
remaining_gap: This checked shell lower bound refutes one proposed closing premise. A genuinely two-sided occupation-decay estimate remains missing.
